series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm/mempolicy: use SRCU for the weighted interleave state
series_items.patch_summary: This patch replaces the current implementation of weighted interleave state management in the Linux kernel's memory policy module with a new approach using SRCU (Schedulable RCU) to pin the global iw_table object and use it in-place. This change allows for more efficient handling of concurrent updates to the weights, reducing the need for synchronization and improving performance. The patch also introduces a new mechanism for retiring the weighted interleave state, which involves calling SRCU for sleeping readers and kfree_rcu for reference-less ones. The changes were tested with various configurations and tools, including KASAN, PROVE_LOCKING, and DEBUG_OBJECTS_RCU_HEAD.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/mempolicy: stop copying the nodemask in the interleave paths
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes the unnecessary copying of a nodemask in interleave node selectors, reducing memory usage and improving performance. The copy was only used to ensure consistency between the node count and the walk, but this is no longer necessary as bounds checking can be used instead. If an empty nodelist or weight is detected, the code falls back to using numa_node_id(). This change also removes a now-unused function read_once_policy_nodemask() and results in significant reductions in stack usage for certain functions.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to eliminate unnecessary copies of nodemasks and node weights in the interleave paths, improving performance by reducing memory allocation and synchronization overhead.

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: Raised a div-by-zero concern in alloc_pages_bulk_interleave() and suggested testing the patch series.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri, 28 Aug 2026 21:59:41 -0400 Gregory Price <gourry@gourry.net> wrote:

> The interleave node selectors and bulk allocators take copies of
> nodemasks and node weights (for weighted interleave) in the fault path.
> Both of these copies can be entirely eliminated.
> 
> For node weights, use SRCU to pin the weights in place.  This eliminates
> a copy and a kmalloc from the bulk allocator path.
> 
> For nodemasks, we can operate directly on pol->nodes as long as we bounds
> check the walk.  A concurrent rebind can shrink the mask, or tear the read
> of it so the mask appears empty.
> 
>  - The interleave node selectors fall back to numa_node_id() when that
>    happens, which is what they already did when a copy came back empty.
> 
>  - The bulk allocator simply returns what it managed to allocate.
> 
> The node count and weight totals are read separately from the nodemask
> walk that consumes them - creating a time-of-check / time-of-use race.
> Just clamp the walk to a single pass (number of nodes), and clamp each
> bulk allocation chunk to the space left in the request.
> 
> The cost is distribution accuracy during a rebind.  The copies never
> corrected for that either - they only kept the code from dividing by
> zero and overrunning the allocation request.

Not very well, it seems.  Sashiko thinks there's a div-by-zero in
alloc_pages_bulk_interleave().

	https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260829015943.1258774-1-gourry@gourry.net

> Gregory Price (2):
>   mm/mempolicy: use SRCU for the weighted interleave state
>   mm/mempolicy: stop copying the nodemask in the interleave paths

Looks nice, thanks - I'll queue it for testing.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] mm/huge_memory: skip zone device folios in madvise_free_huge_pmd()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the madvise_free_huge_pmd() function to skip zone device folios when performing lazyfree operations. The existing guards in this function do not cover all cases of zone device memory, and adding a check for zone device folios ensures that these areas are properly handled. This change addresses an issue where THP migration of zone device pages was not being filtered correctly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] mm/madvise: skip zone device folios in cold/pageout PMD range
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where zone device folios are not properly filtered in the madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range() function, leading to potential double-put bugs. The patch adds a check for zone device memory and skips it during MADV_COLD/PAGEOUT operations.

review_comments.raw_body:

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] mm/mempolicy: skip zone device folios when queueing folios
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where zone device folios are not properly filtered when queueing folios for migration. The patches add explicit checks to skip zone device folios in the `queue_folios_pte_range` and `queue_folios_pmd` functions, ensuring that only valid folios are processed. This fix is necessary because existing checks do not reject zone device memory, leading to incorrect behavior.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series adds missing checks to prevent zone device memory from being reclaimed, aged, or migrated in certain mm walkers. The existing checks only filtered out non-present device-private entries, but did not account for present zone device PMDs. The patches add explicit checks after the folio is resolved and before it is acted upon, ensuring correctness and hardening the kernel against potential issues.

review_comments.author: Lance Yang
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Lance Yang successfully tested the patch series on x86_64 QEMU and confirmed that it fixes a kernel panic issue when using PMD-mapped device-coherent THPs, but noted that without these patches, partial MADV_FREE and MADV_COLD operations would reliably hit a kernel panic in remove_migration_pte()
review_comments.raw_body:
Cool!

Gave the whole series a spin on x86_64 QEMU with a PMD-mapped
device-coherent THP. Without these patches, partial MADV_FREE and
MADV_COLD reliably hit a kernel panic in remove_migration_pte(), while
mbind(MPOL_MF_MOVE | MPOL_MF_STRICT) returned -EIO.

With v2, all three worked fine, PMD mapping stayed intact, and data
checked out :)

Note that both kernels used the same small change to the in-kernel HMM
test driver, allowing its coherent device memory to be allocated as 2 MB
folios so the PMD-mapped test case could be exercised.

Tested-by: Lance Yang <lance.yang@linux.dev>

review_comments.author: Lance Yang
review_comments.summary: Lance Yang noted that the ZONE_DEVICE split handling only covers device-private folios and not device-coherent ones, which are not supported yet; he added checks in folio_check_splittable() and folio_split_unmapped() to reject device-coherent folios with an error code -EOPNOTSUPP.
review_comments.raw_body:
BTW, noticed that the ZONE_DEVICE split handling only covers
device-private folios, so device-coherent folios aren't supported ...

The call chains are:

split_folio()
  -> __folio_split()
    -> folio_check_splittable()
    -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

migrate_vma_pages()
  -> __migrate_device_pages()
    -> migrate_vma_split_unmapped_folio()
      -> folio_split_unmapped()
        -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

And I added the device-coherent check to folio_check_splittable() and
folio_split_unmapped(). See below. They can go away once device-coherent
folio splitting is supported :)

If folks think it's worth having, I can send it as a follow-up :)

---8<---
Subject: [PATCH] mm/huge_memory: don't split device-coherent folios

From: Lance Yang <lance.yang@linux.dev>

The ZONE_DEVICE split handling only covers device-private folios.
Device-coherent folios are not supported.

The call chains are:

split_folio()
  -> __folio_split()
    -> folio_check_splittable()
    -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

migrate_vma_pages()
  -> __migrate_device_pages()
    -> migrate_vma_split_unmapped_folio()
      -> folio_split_unmapped()
        -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

Reject device-coherent folios in folio_check_splittable() and
folio_split_unmapped().

Fixes: a30b48bf1b24 ("mm/migrate_device: implement THP migration of zone device pages")
Signed-off-by: Lance Yang <lance.yang@linux.dev>
---
 mm/huge_memory.c | 14 +++++++++++---
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/huge_memory.c b/mm/huge_memory.c
index 54494c3fa983..a5dd38e9a8de 100644
--- a/mm/huge_memory.c
+++ b/mm/huge_memory.c
@@ -3937,6 +3937,10 @@ int folio_check_splittable(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order,
 	if (!folio->mapping && !folio_test_anon(folio))
 		return -EBUSY;

+	/* TODO: Support splitting device-coherent folios. */
+	if (folio_is_device_coherent(folio))
+		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
+
 	/* order-1 is not supported for anonymous THP. */
 	if (folio_test_anon(folio) && new_order == 1)
 		return -EINVAL;
@@ -4354,15 +4358,16 @@ static int __folio_split(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order,
  *
  * anon_vma_lock is not required to be held, mmap_read_lock() or
  * mmap_write_lock() should be held. @folio is expected to be locked by the
- * caller. device-private and non device-private folios are supported along
+ * caller. device-private and non-ZONE_DEVICE folios are supported along
  * with folios that are in the swapcache. @folio should also be unmapped and
  * isolated from LRU (if applicable)
  *
  * Upon return, the folio is not remapped, split folios are not added to LRU,
  * free_folio_and_swap_cache() is not called, and new folios remain locked.
  *
- * Return: 0 on success, -EAGAIN if the folio cannot be split (e.g., due to
- *         insufficient reference count or extra pins).
+ * Return: 0 on success, -EOPNOTSUPP for device-coherent folios, or -EAGAIN if
+ *         the folio cannot be split (e.g., due to insufficient reference
+ *         count or extra pins).
  */
 int folio_split_unmapped(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order)
 {
@@ -4373,6 +4378,9 @@ int folio_split_unmapped(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order)
 	VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_FOLIO(!folio_test_large(folio), folio);
 	VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_FOLIO(!folio_test_anon(folio), folio);

+	if (folio_is_device_coherent(folio))
+		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
+
 	if (folio_expected_ref_count(folio) != folio_ref_count(folio) - 1)
 		return -EAGAIN;

--

Cheers, Lance

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledges that the split checks are worth it and appreciates the reviewer's testing efforts, indicating no need for further revision.
review_comments.raw_body:
First - thank you for testing, I was struggling to figure out a way to

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 00/14] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener set interface

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 00/14] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener set interface

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 01/14] NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the number of listeners accepted in the listener_set function to prevent a userland request from spinning indefinitely due to an O(N * M) nested loop. The limit is set at NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024), which is considered far above any realistic configuration. The patch also adds a check for oversized listener lists before taking any locks, ensuring that the system remains secure and responsive.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 02/14] NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch validates the transport name in the listener_set function before server creation to prevent arbitrary names from reaching svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). The validation checks if the name matches one of the supported transport classes (tcp, udp, or rdma) and rejects any unsupported names. This narrows the scope of a TASK_KILLABLE usermode helper upcall that can be triggered under nfsd_mutex. The patch also ensures that NFSD accepts 'rdma' without condition, even if svcrdma is not built, to allow for modular autoload in the kernel.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 03/14] SUNRPC: keep the first error in svc_register()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the svc_register() function where it returns the last error encountered, overwriting any earlier failures. Instead, it keeps track of the first error and returns that. This ensures that all errors are preserved and can be reported to the user.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 04/14] SUNRPC: bound the local rpcbind client timeout to 1s
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the timeout for local rpcbind client connections to 1 second. The kernel's current behavior allows a stalled connection to cause a long hold on nfsd_mutex, potentially triggering the hung-task watchdog. By capping the timeout at 1 second, the patch reduces the likelihood of this issue occurring. However, it does not eliminate the problem entirely and registration remains synchronous and fatal. A more comprehensive fix would be to make the registration asynchronous.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 05/14] NFSD: report listener creation failures through extack
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the error reporting in the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) listener creation process by providing more detailed information to userland when a failure occurs. Specifically, it records and reports the attribute and transport name of the entry that failed, allowing for better diagnosis and troubleshooting. The patch modifies the nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit function to set an extack with the relevant error message and details after each loop iteration.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 06/14] SUNRPC: report local rpcbind calls that get no answer
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the SUNRPC system by allowing callers to detect when an rpcbind call fails due to a lack of response, rather than just a refusal. It introduces a new error code -ENAVAIL and modifies the svc_register function to track the number of unanswered calls. The caller can then use this count to determine if there have been errors. This patch also updates various functions and structures to accommodate these changes.

review_comments.author: Chuck Lever
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Chuck Lever noted that rpcb_register_call() incorrectly classifies all failures except -EPROTONOSUPPORT as 'no answer', leading to incorrect counting of failures and loss of syscall-restart semantics on fatal signals, and requested the code be revised to accurately distinguish between different types of failures.
review_comments.raw_body:
If I'm reading this correctly, rpcb_register_call() classifies
every failure except -EPROTONOSUPPORT as "no answer".

rpc_call_sync() returns negative errnos that are not "no answer":
pre-dispatch local failures (-ENOMEM from rpc_new_task()), a fatal
signal (-ERESTARTSYS), and reply-derived errors from
rpc_verify_header(): -EPFNOSUPPORT, -EOPNOTSUPP, -EIO, -EACCES
(auth error), -EKEYREJECTED. All of these show that rpcbind *did*
answer.

Now they become -ENAVAIL, get counted in sv_rpcb_failures, are
silently converted to success for a vs_rpcb_optnl version, and
reach userspace as a synthesized -ETIMEDOUT for mandatory versions.

Consequences:

* The commit message says "-EACCES continues to mean a FALSE
  reply," but the RPC layer's auth -EACCES is rewritten to
  -ENAVAIL before the two can be told apart. Its "one of two
  ways" failure taxonomy is not what the code implements.

* "rpcbind not running" (-ECONNREFUSED/-ENOENT) and every
  other transport error reach nfsd's listener_set ack, the
  svc_register/svc_unregister tracepoints, and the printk
  as indistinguishable ETIMEDOUT/ENAVAIL, which IMO is an
  observability regression.

* -ERESTARTSYS -> -ETIMEDOUT drops syscall-restart semantics
  on a fatal signal during registration.

I'm probably missing something.


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 07/14] SUNRPC: stop svc_register() once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to stop registering programs and versions when the local rpcbind client times out, rather than continuing to try other programs and versions. This change is intended to prevent unnecessary delays and improve performance. The patch achieves this by adding a check for no response from the rpcbind client and breaking out of the program loop if it occurs.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 08/14] SUNRPC: stop the svc_unregister() sweep once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC service to stop clearing rpcbind entries after the first call that receives no answer from rpcbind. This change is intended to prevent unnecessary timeouts and improve performance when a local rpcbind never replies.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 09/14] SUNRPC: stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering. The original behavior caused each listener to wait for a timeout, leading to unnecessary delays and potential failures in the teardown process. To address this issue, the patch introduces a new function `svc_xprt_clear_rpcb_unreg` that clears the flag indicating that rpcbind is unresponsive on remaining listeners when the first failure occurs. This change improves the efficiency of the listener destruction process and reduces the likelihood of further failures during teardown.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 10/14] NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code, where a silent rpcbind failure can cause the nfsd_mutex to be held for an extended period of time. The patch introduces a check for rpcbind failures and, if one occurs, it skips registering with rpcbind for subsequent listeners. This approach prevents the mutex from being held indefinitely and allows the system to recover more quickly in case of a failure.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 11/14] selftests/nfsd: exercise listener_set request validation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds regression tests to the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code to exercise listener_set request validation. The tests cover various invalid scenarios, such as bad transport names, missing addresses, and malformed entries. The tests use a stub to create a service and run in their own network namespace. The patch also updates the MAINTAINERS file and adds new directories to the NFSD test suite.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 12/14] selftests/nfsd: add a per-netns rpcbind stub and the listener round-trips
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-network namespace (netns) rpcbind stub to the selftests/nfsd test suite. The stub serves rpcbind from within the netns, allowing tests to register listeners and round-trip requests without relying on the host's rpcbind service. This is necessary because a fresh netns has no rpcbind service, causing registration failures and timeouts. The patch also includes new tests that cover various scenarios, including listener creation, addition, removal, and IPv6 support.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 13/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener_set asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds tests to the NFS daemon (nfsd) selftest suite to ensure that listener_set requests only ask rpcbind once. The tests cover various scenarios, including stopping a listener after failure, silent set completion, and version set only. New functions are introduced to handle these cases, including RPCB_STUB_SILENT and version_set_only(). The patch aims to prevent multiple calls to rpcbind for each request, which would lead to inefficiencies in the system.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 14/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener removal asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test to ensure that removing multiple listeners from the NFS daemon does not result in multiple timeouts for rpcbind. The test creates one listener, then three listeners while the stub is silent, and measures the number of calls made to rpcbind during each removal. It checks that the second and third removals do not reach rpcbind at all, thus preventing unnecessary timeouts.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series, submitted by Jeff Layton, aims to harden the netlink listener set interface in the NFS daemon and SunRPC code. The main goal is to prevent hangs caused by syzbot, a kernel testing tool. To achieve this, the patches modify the rpcbind registration process to handle failures more robustly. Specifically, when a registration fails, it will no longer leave behind entries that point to closed ports. Additionally, several test cases have been updated to ensure correct behavior in various scenarios. This patch series sets the foundation for further work on moving the rpcbind registration into userland.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the performance impact of a nested loop in nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit(), which can spin for a long time under sv_lock when dealing with large listener lists. The author added a check to reject requests that carry more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024) entries, and explained that this limit is far above any realistic configuration.
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the
existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the
requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock
with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener
list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time.

Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024)
entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code
takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration.

This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets
bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also
holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call
and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case
under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls.
Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

Fixes: 16a471177496 ("NFSD: add listener-{set,get} netlink command")
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
index 5331b89c4281..b6f4d66f612a 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
@@ -1995,21 +1995,22 @@ int nfsd_nl_version_get_doit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	return err;
 }
 
+/* Upper bound on the number of listeners a single request may carry. */
+#define NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX	1024
+
 /**
  * nfsd_nl_validate_listeners - sanity-check the listener list from userland
  * @info: netlink metadata and command arguments
  *
- * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that each entry
- * is well-formed: it parses against the policy, carries both an address and
- * a transport name, and the address is long enough for its family. Doing
- * this up front lets the callers below assume every entry is valid and
- * guarantees we make no changes when the request is malformed.
+ * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that the list is
+ * not oversized and that each entry is well-formed.
  *
  * Return: 0 if every entry is valid, or a negative errno otherwise.
  */
 static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 {
 	const struct nlattr *attr;
+	unsigned int count = 0;
 	int rem;
 
 	nlmsg_for_each_attr_type(attr, NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR, info->nlhdr,
@@ -2018,6 +2019,11 @@ static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 		struct sockaddr *sa;
 		int err;
 
+		if (++count > NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX) {
+			NL_SET_ERR_MSG(info->extack, "too many listeners");
+			return -E2BIG;
+		}
+
 		err = nla_parse_nested(tb, NFSD_A_SOCK_MAX, attr,
 				       nfsd_sock_nl_policy, info->extack);
 		if (err < 0)

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about nfsd_mutex being held for the whole listener teardown and rebuild, explaining that it's necessary to prevent a TASK_KILLABLE usermode helper upcall from running under nfsd_mutex. The author added a check in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners() to reject unsupported transport names before taking nfsd_mutex.
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mutex for the whole listener
teardown and rebuild. The code checks NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME for
presence only, and not for content. An arbitrary name therefore reaches
svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). There, a name that matches no registered class
calls request_module("svc%s", name). That call is a TASK_KILLABLE usermode
helper upcall, and it runs under nfsd_mutex.

Check the name against the classes that NFSD can create: tcp, udp and
rdma. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), which runs before
the code takes nfsd_mutex. The rejection names the offending attribute
through extack, since -EPROTONOSUPPORT on its own does not say which
entry carried the bad name.

This narrows the upcall. It does not remove it. NFSD accepts "rdma"
without a condition, so on a kernel that does not build svcrdma the name
still reaches request_module("svcrdma") under nfsd_mutex. That is
necessary for the modular case, where the autoload is legitimate.

Fixes: 16a471177496 ("NFSD: add listener-{set,get} netlink command")
Assisted-by: LLM
Link: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=c7eae0eb80858a2dba0f
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c | 24 ++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 24 insertions(+)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
index b6f4d66f612a..d8135f38e69f 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
@@ -1995,6 +1995,23 @@ int nfsd_nl_version_get_doit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	return err;
 }
 
+/*
+ * Transport classes NFSD knows how to instantiate. Vetting the name here
+ * keeps a bogus string from reaching svc_xprt_create_from_sa(), where an
+ * unknown name triggers a request_module("svc%s", name) upcall under
+ * nfsd_mutex.
+ */
+static bool nfsd_nl_transport_supported(const char *name)
+{
+	static const char * const supported[] = { "tcp", "udp", "rdma" };
+	int i;
+
+	for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(supported); i++)
+		if (!strcmp(name, supported[i]))
+			return true;
+	return false;
+}
+
 /* Upper bound on the number of listeners a single request may carry. */
 #define NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX	1024
 
@@ -2032,6 +2049,13 @@ static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 		if (!tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_ADDR] || !tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME])
 			return -EINVAL;
 
+		if (!nfsd_nl_transport_supported(nla_data(tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME]))) {
+			NL_SET_ERR_MSG_ATTR(info->extack,
+					    tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME],
+					    "unsupported transport name");
+			return -EPROTONOSUPPORT;
+		}
+
 		sa = nla_data(tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_ADDR]);
 		if (nla_len(tb[NFSD_A_SOCK_ADDR]) < sizeof(sa->sa_family))
 			return -EINVAL;

--

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about svc_register() overwriting earlier registration errors, agreeing to modify the code to keep the first error instead of the last.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern that the local rpcbind client's synchronous calls under nfsd_mutex can cause a long stall, leading to hung-task watchdog warnings. The author explained that shortening the stall by bounding the client's attempts is not a free fix and does not remove the stall entirely; instead, they acknowledged that making registration asynchronous is necessary for a real fix.
review_comments.raw_body:
The kernel's local rpcbind client uses the transport defaults: a 10s major
timeout for AF_LOCAL, and 60s for the loopback TCP fallback.
xprt_calc_majortimeo() returns to_initval when to_increment is 0.

Those calls are synchronous, and they run under nfsd_mutex. One operation
makes several of them. rpcb_create_local() tries up to three client
creations, and svc_register() sends one call for each program and version.
A local rpcbind that accepts the connection but never replies stalls every
one of these calls. The accumulated hold is long enough to trip the
hung-task watchdog on other NFSD netlink operations. The holder itself
waits killably and escapes the watchdog:

  INFO: task hung in nfsd_nl_cache_flush_doit

The local rpcbind is on loopback or on an AF_LOCAL socket, and it answers
in microseconds. Bound its client to one attempt of 1s.

This shortens the stall. It does not remove the stall, and it is not free.
Registration stays synchronous and stays fatal. An rpcb_create_local()
failure aborts nfsd_create_serv() through svc_bind(), and an
svc_register() failure makes svc_setup_socket() fail. An rpcbind that is
merely slow to be scheduled can therefore now fail server startup, where
it succeeded before. The real fix is to make the registration
asynchronous.

Assisted-by: LLM
Link: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=c7eae0eb80858a2dba0f
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c | 12 ++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+)

diff --git a/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c b/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c
index 6aa372188c86..0aa376b82a52 100644
--- a/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c
+++ b/net/sunrpc/rpcb_clnt.c
@@ -221,6 +221,16 @@ static void rpcb_set_local(struct net *net, struct rpc_clnt *clnt,
 # define SUN_LEN(ptr) (offsetof(struct sockaddr_un, sun_path)		\
 		      + 1 + strlen((ptr)->sun_path + 1))
 
+/*
+ * The kernel's rpcbind client talks only to the local rpcbind, over loopback
+ * or a local AF_LOCAL socket, where a healthy rpcbind answers in microseconds.
+ */
+static const struct rpc_timeout rpcb_local_timeout = {
+	.to_initval	= 1 * HZ,
+	.to_maxval	= 1 * HZ,
+	.to_retries	= 0,
+};
+
 /*
  * Returns zero on success, otherwise a negative errno value
  * is returned.
@@ -238,6 +248,7 @@ static int rpcb_create_af_local(struct net *net,
 		.version	= RPCBVERS_2,
 		.authflavor	= RPC_AUTH_NULL,
 		.cred		= current_cred(),
+		.timeout	= &rpcb_local_timeout,
 		/*
 		 * We turn off the idle timeout to prevent the kernel
 		 * from automatically disconnecting the socket.
@@ -312,6 +323,7 @@ static int rpcb_create_local_net(struct net *net)
 		.version	= RPCBVERS_2,
 		.authflavor	= RPC_AUTH_UNIX,
 		.cred		= current_cred(),
+		.timeout	= &rpcb_local_timeout,
 		.flags		= RPC_CLNT_CREATE_NOPING,
 	};
 	struct rpc_clnt *clnt, *clnt4;

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern that the LISTENER_SET operation does not provide enough information to userland when a registration fails, specifically which entry failed. The author added code to record and report the attribute and transport name of the failing entry.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the behavior of svc_register() when an rpcbind registration fails, explaining that it currently waits for each listener individually and cannot learn if the first call already failed. The author proposed introducing a new errno -ENAVAIL to indicate this case, which would be handled differently than existing -EACCES errors.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the inefficiency of svc_register() walking every program and version when an error occurs, explaining that it pays a penalty of twice the timeout time for each program. The author proposed to stop the program loop too when the call gets no answer.
review_comments.raw_body:
svc_register() walks every program and every version. The break on error
leaves the version loop only, so a program whose call to the local rpcbind
timed out is followed by the next program timing out in the same way. With
the 1s bound on the local rpcbind client, an nfsd serv pays 2s for that,
once for nfsd and once for nfsacl.

Stop the program loop too, but only when the call got no answer.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

 net/sunrpc/svc.c | 4 ++++
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+)

--- a/net/sunrpc/svc.c
+++ b/net/sunrpc/svc.c
@@ -1258,6 +1258,10 @@ int svc_register(struct svc_serv *serv, struct net *net,
 				break;
 			}
 		}
+
+		/* Give up on trying to register anything if it didn't respond */
+		if (noanswer)
+			break;
 	}
 
 	if (noanswer)

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the rpcbind entry clearing mechanism in svc_unregister(). They explained that it clears entries for non-hidden programs and versions, and that this results in multiple timeouts under nfsd_mutex when a local rpcbind never replies. The author agreed to give up after the first call that gets no answer.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: Author addressed a concern about rpcbind timeouts during listener set removal, explaining that one failure would trigger the same timeout for all remaining listeners and proposing to clear XPT_RPCB_UNREG on every transport in the same net when the call gets no answer. A fix is planned.

review_comments.author: Chuck Lever
review_comments.summary: The reviewer, Chuck Lever, pointed out that rpcb_register_call() incorrectly classifies all failures except -EPROTONOSUPPORT as 'no answer', leading to incorrect handling of errors such as -ENOMEM, -ERESTARTSYS, and auth-related errors. He noted that these errors should be treated differently from 'no answer' cases, which are silently converted to success for vs_rpcb_optnl versions.
review_comments.raw_body:
If I'm reading this correctly, rpcb_register_call() classifies
every failure except -EPROTONOSUPPORT as "no answer".

rpc_call_sync() returns negative errnos that are not "no answer":
pre-dispatch local failures (-ENOMEM from rpc_new_task()), a fatal
signal (-ERESTARTSYS), and reply-derived errors from
rpc_verify_header(): -EPFNOSUPPORT, -EOPNOTSUPP, -EIO, -EACCES
(auth error), -EKEYREJECTED. All of these show that rpcbind *did*
answer.

Now they become -ENAVAIL, get counted in sv_rpcb_failures, are
silently converted to success for a vs_rpcb_optnl version, and
reach userspace as a synthesized -ETIMEDOUT for mandatory versions.

Consequences:

* The commit message says "-EACCES continues to mean a FALSE
  reply," but the RPC layer's auth -EACCES is rewritten to
  -ENAVAIL before the two can be told apart. Its "one of two
  ways" failure taxonomy is not what the code implements.

* "rpcbind not running" (-ECONNREFUSED/-ENOENT) and every
  other transport error reach nfsd's listener_set ack, the
  svc_register/svc_unregister tracepoints, and the printk
  as indistinguishable ETIMEDOUT/ENAVAIL, which IMO is an
  observability regression.

* -ERESTARTSYS -> -ETIMEDOUT drops syscall-restart semantics
  on a fatal signal during registration.

I'm probably missing something.


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)
